newsitem.title: USA: U.S. sends Cubans home, rafters' numbers surge.
newsitem.headline: U.S. sends Cubans home, rafters' numbers surge.

text.p: Twenty Cuban boat people were repatriated on Tuesday as the U.S. Coast Guard contended with a summer surge of Cubans fleeing the communist-ruled Caribbean island.
Fifty-four Cuban migrants were intercepted in the first week of July, more than any month this year, officials said. A total of 183 had been intercepted to date.
Cubans in small boats and makeshift rafts set out on the 100-mile (160-km) journey across the Florida Straits in hopes of reaching the United States.
"Typically you see more migrants in the summer months due to better weather," Coast Guard Petty Officer Scott Carr said.
Barring hurricanes, the passage is less dangerous in the summer when winds ease and seas are generally calm.
Those sent back to Cuba on Tuesday were among 41 migrants intercepted in the waters of the Bahamas and the Florida Keys during the weekend, the Coast Guard said.

Twelve were found in two groups near Anguilla Cay, Bahamas on Friday and seven others were found nearby on Saturday. A woman suffering from possible appendicitis was flown to a hospital in the Florida Keys and the remaining 18 were handed over to Bahamian authorities in Freeport.
On Saturday, a group of 13 Cubans was spotted north of Anguilla and another of nine was found 30 miles (50 km) southeast of Long Key, Florida.
Two Cubans were taken to the U.S. Navy Base at Guantanamo Bay, Cuba for immigration screening while the other 20 were repatriated.
The U.S. returns rafters to Cuba under a 1995 migration accord between Washington and Havana that reversed a decades-old open-door policy toward Cubans fleeing Fidel Castro's regime.
